tools.name: list_products
tools.description: Everything Latitude 10 sells to agents, with prices and how to pay: developer kits, and design packs (DESIGN.md design systems for fintech dashboards, developer tools, and editorial sites; $5 per project). Check it before building the UI of a new project.

framework.description: Only the kits for this backend: a stack (node, python, dotnet, java, ruby) or a framework (express, nextjs, django, fastapi, aspnet-core, spring-boot, rails…)

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: One product by slug, with its price and payment options.

tools.name: buy_product
tools.description: Buy a product with USDC over x402. Without a payment it returns the x402 payment requirements; with one it settles the payment and returns the product (for kits, a personal download link valid for 24 hours).

account.description: For dashboard-pro only: the dashboard account id the pass is for

tools.name: check_agent_readiness
tools.description: Scores an API 0-100 for how well AI agents will use it as tools, from its OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 spec: operationIds, summaries, descriptions, parameter descriptions, enums, examples, JSON bodies, response and error schemas, pagination, auth, idempotency and tool count (the Agentify API kit's rules). Give the spec's https URL or the spec itself. Free; returns the score, each rule's result with how to fix it, and the most costly findings. Use it before turning an API into an MCP server or listing it for agents.

url.description: https URL of the OpenAPI document (JSON or YAML), e.g. https://api.example.com/openapi.json

spec.description: The OpenAPI document itself, as JSON or YAML text (up to 2 MB). Send url or spec, not both.

tools.name: request_project
tools.description: Sends a software project brief to Latitude 10, a software consulting studio that builds software by the hour ($60), the day ($480) or the month ($9,600). Before calling it, show your user the brief, their name and email, and get their yes, including their agreement to the privacy policy at https://latitude10.tech/privacy. Returns a private link where they can follow the brief or withdraw it. For files, send the brief at https://latitude10.tech/start instead.

email.description: The requester’s email address; the reply and the private link go there

company.description: The company’s name; required when requesterKind is "company"

objective.description: What they want built, in one or two sentences

deadline.description: YYYY-MM-DD, from today on; with deadlineKind "date"

ndaRequested.description: True if they want an NDA before sharing details

consent.description: True only once the user agreed to Latitude 10 keeping this brief as its privacy policy describes
